title: Canada GDP by industry, May 2026
question: What will Statistics Canada first report as the month-over-month percent change in seasonally adjusted real gross domestic product by industry, all industries, at basic prices, for May 2026?
resolutionSource: Statistics Canada The Daily release and Table 36-10-0434-01
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first Statistics Canada publication for May 2026 seasonally adjusted real GDP by industry, all industries, month-to-month percent change, rounded to one decimal percentage point. Use the first value published in the July 31, 2026 The Daily release and Table 36-10-0434-01; if the Daily text and table disagree at first publication, use the table value for all industries month-to-month percent change. Ignore later revisions.
drivers: Statistics Canada advance estimate points to 0.1 percent May growth
April's 0.5 percent rebound creates some payback risk
Finance and insurance and real estate support modest growth
Wholesale trade and agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting are cited offsets
Recent first prints remain centered around low positive growth

reasoning.text: Forecast for Canada May 2026 real GDP by industry monthly growth

Framing and exact resolver: this targets Statistics Canada's first print for seasonally adjusted real GDP by industry, all industries, at basic prices, month-over-month percent change for May 2026. The target is the official July 31, 2026 May release, not the June 30 advance estimate and not later revised history.

reasoning.call: Checked Statistics Canada 2026-2027 major economic release dates PDF for Gross domestic product by industry.
reasoning.result: Fetched schedule values: Gross domestic product by industry is scheduled for June 30, 2026 for April 2026, July 31, 2026 for May 2026, and August 28, 2026 for June 2026.

reasoning.call: Fetched Statistics Canada The Daily release for Gross domestic product by industry, April 2026.
reasoning.result: Fetched April 2026 official context: real GDP by industry increased 0.5% in April after March -0.1%; goods-producing industries rose 1.2%, services-producing industries rose 0.3%, and 14 of 20 industrial sectors grew.

reasoning.call: Read the April 2026 GDP by industry Daily release section giving Statistics Canada's advance estimate for May 2026.
reasoning.result: Fetched May 2026 advance estimate: real GDP by industry increased 0.1%; finance and insurance and real estate and rental and leasing increased, while wholesale trade and agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting decreased; Statistics Canada said the May estimate would be updated on July 31, 2026.

reasoning.call: Fetched recent official GDP by industry first-print Daily releases for December 2025 through March 2026.
reasoning.result: Fetched recent first prints: December 2025 = 0.2%, January 2026 = 0.1%, February 2026 = 0.2%, and March 2026 = -0.1% for real GDP by industry monthly growth.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: the recent official first-print reference class for the exact monthly all-industries GDP-by-industry series is low positive growth. The December-April prints of 0.2, 0.1, 0.2, -0.1, and 0.5 average 0.18 percent, while the median is 0.2 percent; including the official May advance estimate pulls the center toward 0.1 percent.

Level, momentum, one-off, and policy mechanisms: the level signal improved sharply in April, but April's 0.5 percent gain had catch-up elements in oil and gas, manufacturing, transportation, and construction. May momentum is still positive but clearly slower in the official advance estimate. The one-off risk is payback after April's rebound. Policy and external mechanisms remain mixed: trade and tariff uncertainty drag on wholesale and goods activity, while finance, real estate, and public-facing services support a modest positive print.

Prior/update/interval: prior model is latest-advance/persistence blended with the recent official first-print reference class from December 2025 through April 2026. I start from the 0.1 May advance estimate, add +0.05 percentage point for finance and real estate support, subtract -0.05 for wholesale/agriculture weakness and April payback, and keep the rounded point at 0.1. The 80% interval method uses realized recent first-print dispersion plus advance-estimate miss risk, widened for one-decimal rounding and sector payback, producing -0.2 to 0.4.

Counter-consideration: downside risk is that April's rebound was mostly temporary catch-up and May wholesale, agriculture, or goods output weakness pulls the first print below zero. Upside risk is that finance, real estate, energy, and services strength were understated by the advance estimate. A print at or below -0.2 would land below the interval; a print at or above 0.4 would land above the interval.

Point calculation: May advance estimate 0.1 + 0.05 finance/real-estate support - 0.05 wholesale/agriculture and April-payback drag = 0.10, rounded to 0.1. Interval calculation: center 0.1 minus 0.3 percentage point = -0.2, and center 0.1 plus 0.3 percentage point = 0.4, giving an 80% rounded first-print interval.
